### Phillips Edison & Company Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


October 26, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s204.q4cdn.com/188135007/files/doc_news/Phillips-Edison--Company-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf)


CINCINNATI, Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Phillips Edison & Company, Inc. (Nasdaq: PECO) (“PECO” or the “Company”), one of the nation’s largest owners and operators of high-quality, grocery-anchored neighborhood shopping centers, today reported financial and operating results for the period ended September 30, 2026 and provided updated 2026 earnings guidance. For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, net income attributable to stockholders was $62.7 million, or $0.49 per diluted share, and $134.2 million, or $1.05 per diluted share, respectively.


**Highlights for the** **Third** **Quarter**


- Reported Nareit FFO of $0.69 per diluted share, representing 7.8% year-over-year growth
- Reported Core FFO of $0.71 per diluted share, representing 9.2% year-over-year growth
- Increased same-center NOI year-over-year by 5.3%
- The increased midpoint of full year 2026 Nareit FFO per diluted share guidance of $2.70 represents 6.3% year-over-year growth
- The increased midpoint of full year 2026 Core FFO per diluted share guidance of $2.77 represents 6.5% year-over-year growth
- The increased midpoint of full year 2026 same-center NOI guidance represents 3.75% year-over-year growth
- Full year 2026 gross acquisitions guidance reflects a range of $600 million to $700 million
- Acquired two grocery-anchored shopping centers, one Everyday Retail™ center and land parcels for a total of $181.8 million and sold $87.1 million in assets
- Reported strong leased portfolio occupancy of 97.5% and same-center leased portfolio occupancy of 97.8%
- Reported leased anchor occupancy of 99.0% and same-center leased anchor occupancy of 99.2%
- Reported leased inline occupancy of 95.1% and same-center leased inline occupancy of 95.4%
- Executed comparable portfolio new and inline leases at a rent spread of 26.3% during the quarter
- Executed comparable portfolio renewal leases at a record rent spread of 25.2% and comparable inline renewal leases at a record-high rent spread of 24.2% during the quarter
- Generated net proceeds of $6.4 million through the issuance of 0.2 million common shares at a gross weighted average price of $42.20 per common share through PECO’s ATM program
- Trailing 12-month net debt to annualized adjusted EBITDA *re* at September 30, 2026 was 5.2x


**Subsequent Highlights**


- Acquired two grocery-anchored shopping centers for $59.4 million at PECO’s total prorated share and sold a land parcel for $0.9 million
- Year to date through October 26, 2026, acquired $519.1 million in assets at PECO’s total prorated share and sold $174.8 million in assets
- Expanded and extended by 10 years the joint venture partnership with Northwestern Mutual to acquire 13 high-quality, grocery-anchored shopping centers valued at approximately $377.5 million and currently owned and operated by PECO across eight states
- Closed on a new $350 million unsecured term loan with a portion of proceeds used to pay down the $162 million term loan due January 2027, lowering the interest rate by approximately 30 basis points


**Management Commentary**


Jeff Edison, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of PECO stated: “PECO delivered another quarter of strong financial results, and the operating environment remains solid. Our record renewal rent spreads and high occupancy showcase the strength of PECO’s operating engine. PECO combines right-sized and well-located, grocery-anchored neighborhood shopping centers that support successful necessity-based retailers with a team that converts retailer demand into durable internal growth.”


Edison added: “We continue to match fund our external growth by selling stabilized centers and investing in centers with greater growth potential. Our leasing relationships, operating platform and market data give us a meaningful advantage when executing acquisitions. The embedded growth, together with our disciplined approach to investing, position PECO well for 2027 and beyond.”


**Financial Results**


*Net Income*


Third quarter 2026 net income attributable to stockholders totaled $62.7 million, or $0.49 per diluted share, compared to net income of $24.7 million, or $0.20 per diluted share, during the third quarter of 2025.


For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net income attributable to stockholders totaled $134.2 million, or $1.05 per diluted share, compared to net income of $63.8 million, or $0.51 per diluted share, for the same period in 2025.


*Nareit FFO*


Third quarter 2026 funds from operations attributable to stockholders and operating partnership (“OP”) unit holders as defined by Nareit (“Nareit FFO”) increased 9.8% to $98.0 million, or $0.69 per diluted share, compared to $89.3 million, or $0.64 per diluted share, during the third quarter of 2025.


For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Nareit FFO increased 7.7% to $284.6 million, or $2.03 per diluted share, compared to $264.3 million, or $1.90 per diluted share, during the same period in 2025.


*Core FFO*


Third quarter 2026 core funds from operations attributable to stockholders and OP unit holders (“Core FFO”) increased 11.3% to $100.7 million, or $0.71 per diluted share, compared to $90.6 million, or $0.65 per diluted share, during the third quarter of 2025.


For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Core FFO increased 8.6% to $292.6 million, or $2.09 per diluted share, compared to $269.5 million, or $1.94 per diluted share, for the same period in 2025.


*Same-Center NOI*


Third quarter 2026 same-center net operating income (“NOI”) increased 5.3% to $122.4 million, compared to $116.2 million during the third quarter of 2025.


For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, same-center NOI increased 4.3% to $361.8 million, compared to $346.9 million during the same period in 2025.


**Portfolio Overview**


*Portfolio Statistics*


As of September 30, 2026, PECO’s wholly-owned portfolio consisted of 300 properties, totaling approximately 33.9 million square feet, located in 31 states. This compared to 303 properties, totaling approximately 34.0 million square feet, located in 31 states as of September 30, 2025.


Leased portfolio occupancy was 97.5% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 97.6% as of September 30, 2025. Same-center leased portfolio occupancy was 97.8% as of September 30, 2026 and 2025.


Leased anchor occupancy was 99.0% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 99.2% as of September 30, 2025. Same-center leased anchor occupancy was 99.2% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 99.4% as of September 30, 2025.


Leased inline occupancy was 95.1% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 94.8% as of September 30, 2025. Same-center leased inline occupancy was 95.4% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 95.0% as of September 30, 2025.


*Leasing Activity*


During the third quarter of 2026, 238 leases were executed totaling approximately 1.1 million square feet. This compared to 270 leases executed totaling approximately 1.7 million square feet during the third quarter of 2025.


For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, 788 leases were executed totaling approximately 3.9 million square feet. This compared to 780 leases executed totaling approximately 4.6 million square feet during the same period in 2025.


During the third quarter of 2026, comparable rent spreads, which represent the percentage increase of a lease to the expiring lease of a unit that was occupied within the past twelve months, were a record-high 25.2% for renewal leases, 26.3% for new leases and 25.5% combined.


Comparable rent spreads during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were 32.3% for new leases, 22.3% for renewal leases and 24.9% combined.


*Transaction Activity - Wholly-Owned*


During the third quarter of 2026, the Company acquired $181.8 million in assets, which included three shopping centers and land parcels. The Company expects to drive value in these assets through occupancy increases and rent growth, as well as potential future development of ground-up outparcel retail spaces.


The third quarter 2026 acquisitions included:


- South Shore Commons, a 157,574 square foot Everyday Retail™ center located in Staten Island, New York.
- Alafaya Square, a 168,532 square foot shopping center anchored by Publix located in an Orlando, Florida suburb.
- Easton Commons, a 203,728 square foot shopping center anchored by Kroger located in a Houston, Texas suburb.


During the same period, the Company sold $87.1 million in assets, which included five shopping centers and a land parcel.


For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company acquired $448.7 million in assets, which included 13 shopping centers and land parcels. During the same period, $174.0 million in assets were sold, which included nine shopping centers and land parcels.


Subsequent to quarter end, the Company acquired $52.8 million in assets, which included:


- Rice Lake Square, a 258,525 square foot shopping center anchored by Pete’s Fresh Market located in a Chicago, Illinois suburb.


Subsequent to quarter end, the Company sold a land parcel for $0.9 million.


*Transaction Activity - Joint Venture*


For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company acquired $11.0 million in assets at PECO’s total prorated share, which included one shopping center and one outparcel.


Subsequent to quarter end, the Company acquired $6.6 million in assets at PECO’s total prorated share, which included:


- Memorial Commons, a 111,022 square foot shopping center anchored by Harris Teeter located in a Charlotte, North Carolina suburb, acquired through Neighborhood Grocery Catalyst Fund LLC.


The Company previously announced on October 1, 2026 an amended and restated joint venture partnership with Northwestern Mutual, one of the largest commercial real estate mortgage and equity investors in the U.S., which extends the term of the venture, Grocery Retail Partners I LLC (“GRP I”), by 10 years to 2036. The expanded joint venture will acquire 13 high-quality, grocery-anchored shopping centers currently owned and operated by PECO across eight states. Northwestern Mutual and PECO will retain approximately 86% and 14% interest in the joint venture, respectively. PECO will continue to provide leasing, asset management and property management services for the joint venture, in addition to earning recurring fees related to these services.


**Balance Sheet Highlights**


Subsequent to quarter end, the Company closed on a new $350 million unsecured term loan facility. The term loan facility has a three-year term maturing on October 23, 2029 and will initially bear interest at an annual rate of SOFR plus 0.80%, with future pricing subject to adjustment based on the Company's credit ratings and leverage ratio. Phillips Edison Grocery Center Operating Partnership I, L.P., a subsidiary of the Company and the borrower under the term loan facility (the “Borrower”), borrowed $175 million of the term loan facility at closing with the remaining $175 million available to draw on or before April 21, 2027. The term loan also has an uncommitted accordion feature allowing the Borrower to borrow up to an additional $450 million of term loans, for total term loans of up to $800 million. The Borrower has the ability to prepay the term loan under the facility without premium or penalty any time prior to maturity. Proceeds from the initial $175 million borrowing were used to pay down the Borrower's outstanding $161.8 million term loan along with outstanding balances under its $1 billion revolving credit facility.


As of September 30, 2026, the Company had approximately $762 million of total liquidity, comprised of $17.9 million of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, plus $744.3 million of borrowing capacity available on its $1.0 billion revolving credit facility. Pro forma for the new $350 million unsecured term loan, the Company had approximately $950 million of total liquidity.


As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s net debt to adjusted EBITDA *re* was 5.2x on a trailing twelve month basis and 5.0x on a current quarter annualized basis, which compares to 5.2x and 5.1x, respectively, as of December 31, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s outstanding debt had a weighted-average interest rate of 4.5% and a weighted-average maturity of 5.3 years when including all extension options, and 85.2% of the Company’s total debt was fixed-rate debt, which includes PECO’s total prorated share of debt for its joint ventures.


During the third quarter of 2026, the Company generated net proceeds of $6.4 million through the issuance of 0.2 million common shares at a gross weighted average price of $42.20 per common share through PECO’s ATM program. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company generated net proceeds of $91.7 million through the issuance of 2.2 million common shares at a gross weighted average price of $42.07 per common share through PECO’s ATM program.


The Company’s interest rate swap with a notional value of $200 million and a fixed rate of 3.359% expired on September 1, 2026.

**About Phillips Edison & Company**


Phillips Edison & Company, Inc. (“PECO”) is one of the nation’s largest owners and operators of high-quality, grocery-anchored neighborhood shopping centers. Founded in 1991, PECO has generated strong results through its vertically-integrated operating platform and national footprint of well-occupied shopping centers. PECO’s centers feature a mix of national and regional retailers providing necessity-based goods and services in fundamentally strong markets throughout the United States. PECO’s top grocery anchors include Kroger, Publix, Albertsons and Ahold Delhaize. As of September 30, 2026, PECO managed 328 shopping centers, including 300 wholly-owned centers comprising 33.9 million square feet across 31 states and 28 shopping centers owned in three institutional joint ventures. PECO is focused on creating great grocery-anchored shopping experiences and improving communities, one neighborhood shopping center at a time.

**Discussion and Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures** ***Same-Center Net Operating Income***


The Company presents Same-Center NOI as a supplemental measure of its performance. The Company defines NOI as total operating revenues, adjusted to exclude non-cash revenue items and lease buyout income, less property operating expenses and real estate taxes. For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, Same-Center NOI represents the NOI for the 275 properties that were wholly-owned for the entirety of both calendar year periods being compared. The Company believes Same-Center NOI provides useful information to its investors about its financial and operating performance because it provides a performance measure of the revenues and expenses directly involved in owning and operating real estate assets and provides a perspective not immediately apparent from net income (loss). Because Same-Center NOI excludes the change in NOI from properties acquired or disposed of after December 31, 2024, it highlights operating trends such as occupancy levels, rental rates, and operating costs for the Company’s same-center portfolio. Other REITs may use different methodologies for calculating Same-Center NOI, and accordingly, PECO’s Same-Center NOI may not be comparable to other REITs.


Same-Center NOI should not be viewed as an alternative measure of the Company’s financial performance as it does not reflect the operations of its entire portfolio, nor does it reflect the impact of general and administrative expenses, depreciation and amortization, interest expense, other income (expense), or the level of capital expenditures and leasing costs necessary to maintain the operating performance of the Company’s properties that could materially impact its results from operations.


***Nareit Funds from Operations and Core Funds from Operations***


Nareit FFO is a non-GAAP financial performance measure that is widely recognized as a measure of REIT operating performance. The National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts (“Nareit”) defines FFO as net income (loss) computed in accordance with GAAP, excluding: (i) gains (or losses) from sales of property and gains (or losses) from change in control; (ii) depreciation and amortization related to real estate; and (iii) impairment losses on real estate and impairments of in-substance real estate investments in investees that are driven by measurable decreases in the fair value of the depreciable real estate held by the unconsolidated partnerships and joint ventures. Adjustments for unconsolidated partnerships and joint ventures are calculated to reflect Nareit FFO on the same basis. The Company calculates Nareit FFO in a manner consistent with the Nareit definition.


Core FFO is an additional financial performance measure used by the Company as Nareit FFO includes certain non-comparable items that affect its performance over time. The Company believes that Core FFO is helpful in assisting management and investors with the assessment of the sustainability of operating performance in future periods, and that it is more reflective of its core operating performance and provides an additional measure to compare PECO’s performance across reporting periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that may cause short-term fluctuations in net income (loss). To arrive at Core FFO, the Company adjusts Nareit FFO to exclude certain recurring and non-recurring items including, but not limited to: (i) depreciation and amortization of corporate assets; (ii) changes in the fair value of the earn-out liability; (iii) adjustments related to its investments in unconsolidated joint ventures; (iv) gains or losses on the extinguishment or modification of debt and other; (v) other impairment charges; (vi) transaction and acquisition expenses; and (vii) realized performance income.


Nareit FFO and Core FFO should not be considered alternatives to net income (loss) under GAAP, as an indication of the Company’s liquidity, nor as an indication of funds available to cover its cash needs, including its ability to fund distributions. Core FFO may not be a useful measure of the impact of long-term operating performance on value if the Company does not continue to operate its business plan in the manner currently contemplated.


Accordingly, Nareit FFO and Core FFO should be reviewed in connection with other GAAP measurements, and should not be viewed as more prominent measures of performance than net income (loss) or cash flows from operations prepared in accordance with GAAP. The Company’s Nareit FFO and Core FFO, as presented, may not be comparable to amounts calculated by other REITs.


***Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization for Real Estate and Adjusted EBITDAre***


Nareit defines Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization for Real Estate (“EBITDA *re* ”) as net income (loss) computed in accordance with GAAP before: (i) interest expense; (ii) income tax expense; (iii) depreciation and amortization; (iv) gains or losses from disposition of depreciable property; and (v) impairment write-downs of depreciable property. Adjustments for unconsolidated partnerships and joint ventures are calculated to reflect EBITDA *re* on the same basis.


Adjusted EBITDA *re* is an additional performance measure used by the Company as EBITDA *re* includes certain non-comparable items that affect the Company’s performance over time. To arrive at Adjusted EBITDA *re,* the Company excludes certain recurring and non-recurring items from EBITDA *re* , including, but not limited to: (i) changes in the fair value of the earn-out liability; (ii) other impairment charges; (iii) adjustments related to its investments in unconsolidated joint ventures; (iv) transaction and acquisition expenses; and (v) realized performance income.


The Company uses EBITDA *re* and Adjusted EBITDA *re* as additional measures of operating performance which allow it to compare earnings independent of capital structure, determine debt service and fixed cost coverage, and measure enterprise value. Additionally, the Company believes they are a useful indicator of its ability to support its debt obligations. EBITDA *re* and Adjusted EBITDA *re* should not be considered as alternatives to net income (loss), as an indication of the Company’s liquidity, nor as an indication of funds available to cover its cash needs, including its ability to fund distributions.
